success_patterns: The agent split the five options into a hub plus single edits. The hub was 'an explicit metric exists whose topology is exactly the Bowman topology'. A was the bare-membership truncation (metrizable). B and C added construction-detail riders ('only finitely many weighted projection terms', 'using only a metric on E(S), without any auxiliary metrics from the G_e'). D replaced the stem's defined topology with the original topology.

It treated 'explicit metric compatible with the Bowman topology' as a legitimate upgrade over bare 'metrizable'. The extra content is stated in the stem's own objects, keeps every hypothesis, and is the natural constructive form of the theorem.

It rejected B and C because their extra clauses were unprovable restrictions on how the metric is built. Both ignore the hypothesis that each G_e is compact metrizable and that the functor preserves inverse limits, so they are the 'only / without / finitely many' downgrade-or-inflation corruption. A construction that must use the G_e metrics is the natural reading.

It rejected D because it replaces the stem's defined object (the Bowman topology) with a different topology and asserts they coincide. This is an unconditional new phenomenon that the hypotheses do not give.
It committed to the plain option once it was the unique survivor: not false, not a corollary of another survivor, and with no unjustified rider.
